title: An entire automotive stamping plant: lines, PLCs, networks, maintenance crews
summary: A hierarchical map of a fictional stamping plant — from the front gate down through lines, controls, networks, and the crews who keep steel moving.

blocks.title: One plant, five layers deep
blocks.body: Fictional Riverbend Stampings presses automotive body panels across three press lines. This page is a navigation map: plant → lines → controls → network → crews. Nothing here is a real OEM's confidential layout — it is a teaching plant you can hold in your head.

blocks.title: Fictional plant
blocks.body: Riverbend Stampings, its line names, IP schemes, and crew rosters are invented for this artifact. Use it to learn hierarchy, not to reverse-engineer a real site.

blocks.heading: Riverbend as a system
blocks.body: Coil steel enters on the north dock, blanks move to press lines, finished panels leave on the south docks toward assembly plants. Compressed air, 480 V distribution, and process water are shared utilities. The quality lab sits between Lines B and C so auditors walk less. The plant's job is cadence: dies change, steel grades change, but the hierarchy stays so a new tech can find the right cabinet.

blocks.heading: Plant-level rooms that matter
rows: Crane + coil cars; not a tourist zone
Hearing protection; red pathways for die moves
Huge travel paths — schedule conflicts with production

columns.name: Line A — Blanking
columns.detail: Coil to blanks. Faster cadence, simpler dies, feeds B and C. Downtime here starves everyone.

columns.name: Line B — Transfer press
columns.detail: Major body panels. Multi-station transfer; die changes are planned like pit stops.

columns.name: Line C — Transfer press
columns.detail: Sister to B with different die set. Often runs the overflow / alternate part family.

blocks.heading: What "the line is up" actually means
items: Coil or blank stacked and verified for the active die recipe.
Die in press, clamps confirmed, shut height and counterbalance set per sheet.
Automation (transfer / robots) homed with clear aisle photos or light curtains healthy.
First-off quality check signed before rate production.
End-of-line racking and scrap conveyors not backed up into the press envelope.

nodes.title: Safety PLC
nodes.detail: Light curtains, e-stops, gate locks — independent of convenience logic.

nodes.title: Line PLC
nodes.detail: Sequence, transfer timing, fault handling, recipe select.

nodes.title: Press / drive controllers
nodes.detail: Main motor, slide, transfer servos — often vendor islands with handshake bits.

nodes.title: HMIs
nodes.detail: Operator stations at feed, press, and end-of-line.

blocks.heading: Networks as a hierarchy too
blocks.body: Cell networks on each line stay close to the I/O and drives. A plant backbone carries historian traffic, recipe distribution, and supervised remote access. The serious rule: operator convenience VLANs do not casually bridge into safety or motion segments. When someone says "the network is down," ask which layer — cell switch, backbone, or the laptop VPN path into the MTR.

blocks.heading: Example network layers
rows: PLC IO, drive cyclic data, local HMI

blocks.title: Remote access is a procedure, not a port
blocks.body: Fictional Riverbend requires a ticket, a time window, and a named escort for vendor VPNs. That policy is part of the hierarchy — same as a lockout.

columns.name: Production
columns.detail: Runs rate, calls stops, owns first response on jams within training.

columns.name: Die set / tooling
columns.detail: Die changes, shut height, panel quality tied to die condition.

columns.name: Electrical / controls
columns.detail: PLCs, drives, networks, safety devices — with LOTO still mandatory.

blocks.heading: Hierarchy check
blocks.prompt: A light curtain fault on Line C is primarily which layer's device, even though the HMI lives on the network?
blocks.explanation: Safety devices and the safety PLC are controls-layer assets. Networks may report the fault; they are not the curtain itself.
blocks.correctFeedback: Yes — safety devices sit in controls, with safety PLC ownership.
blocks.wrongFeedback: Use the layer map: curtains → safety PLC → controls layer.
